scenes.problem: Find √36. Show why your answer is the principal square root.
rows: Read √36 as the nonnegative number whose square is 36.
Build a square with 36 equal unit tiles.
Arrange the tiles into 6 rows of 6 tiles.
The side count is 6; 6 × 6 = 36.
Therefore √36 = 6; the √ sign asks for the nonnegative root.
scenes.misconception: The principal √ is nonnegative; check by squaring the proposed side.

scenes.problem: Find ∛64. Show the three equal dimensions.
rows: Read ∛64 as the number that gives 64 when cubed.
Build a cube from 64 equal unit cubes.
Count 4 unit cubes along each of the three edges.
Therefore ∛64 = 4.
scenes.misconception: Cube root asks for three equal factors, not division by three.

scenes.problem: Evaluate √81 + ∛125. Show the two roots separately.
rows: Keep √81 and ∛125 separate: their indices describe different shapes.
Arrange 81 tiles into a 9 by 9 square, so √81 = 9.
Arrange 125 cubes into a 5 by 5 by 5 cube, so ∛125 = 5.
Substitute the two root values: 9 + 5.
Add to obtain 14.
scenes.misconception: Evaluate each root with its own index before adding.

scenes.problem: A square has area 169 cm². Find its side length and perimeter.
rows: Label the equal sides s. Area = s × s = 169 cm².
Take the nonnegative square root: s = √169.
Arrange 169 square centimetres in a 13 by 13 square.
So the side length is 13 cm.
The perimeter is four sides: 4 × 13 = 52 cm.
scenes.memo: 13 × 13 = 169 cm², and four sides total 52 cm.
scenes.misconception: Area has square units, perimeter has linear units; a square has four equal sides.

scenes.problem: A cube has volume 343 cm³. Find one edge length.
rows: Label all three equal edges s; volume = s × s × s.
Therefore s³ = 343 cm³.
Take the cube root: s = ∛343.
Build 7 equal layers, each 7 by 7 unit cubes.
The edge is 7 cm.
scenes.misconception: Volume counts three equal dimensions; an edge uses linear units.
